0266d366-dec6-4bd1-8a2f-76386846dfba.title: Hedley Foundation — Small Grants
0266d366-dec6-4bd1-8a2f-76386846dfba.description: Small grants £250–£5,000 (typical £2k–£3k) to UK charities for projects benefiting young people — including youth, sport, arts, training, disability and health. Four rounds per year; can't reapply within two years of a successful grant. Income cap ~£1m.

funder_brief.exclusions: Applications for core salaries, building construction, general running costs, transport, financial deficits, or overseas projects. Community interest companies, religious institutions, museums, and individuals are not eligible.
funder_brief.priorities: Charities demonstrating clear, measurable impact and quantifiable outcomes for their beneficiaries.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Be concise and specific about impact. Ensure all contact details (email and phone) are correct. Include your most recent accounts and a recent bank statement — these are essential to a complete application.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Download the application form (available in Word or PDF), complete it with supporting documents, and email to applications@hedleyfoundation.org.uk or post to Lucy Janes, Appeals Secretary, The Hedley Foundation, 1-3 College Hill, London EC4R 2RA.
funder_brief.typical_award: Grants typically range from £250 to £5,000, with occasional larger awards where high impact can be demonstrated.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Small UK registered charities with an annual income below £1 million. Community interest companies, religious institutions, museums, and individuals cannot apply. You must not have received a grant from The Hedley Foundation within the last two years.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Projects and activities that deliver quantifiable, measurable outcomes for beneficiaries. The foundation supports a broad range of charitable work across sectors.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Trustees meet regularly to review applications. If you do not hear within four months, assume your application was unsuccessful. The foundation is unable to respond to queries about submitted applications.
funder_brief.strong_application: Show clear, measurable outcomes and state exactly who will benefit and how many people. Include a detailed cost breakdown, accurate contact details, recent accounts (Statement of Financial Activities with Balance Sheet), and a recent bank statement showing account number and sort code. Keep your application concise.

040888ac-bdd1-4a22-9f33-cc841f9b5cbb.title: Backstage Trust — Performing Arts Grants
040888ac-bdd1-4a22-9f33-cc841f9b5cbb.description: Grants to UK registered charities and Community Interest Companies in the performing arts, with particular focus on theatre and music. Supports youth involvement, community participation in live arts, professional development for small/medium arts organisations, freelance performing-arts workers, new writing, and capital projects. Applications are rolling; grants have reached up to £500,000.

funder_brief.priorities: Accessibility; diversity; youth engagement; new writing; professional development.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Safeguarding policy is a hard requirement — have it in place before applying.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: The Trust does not operate a website. Request the Information Pack via the listing at fundingforall.org.uk and apply directly. Applications are rolling.
funder_brief.typical_award: No fixed range; grants up to £500,000.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: UK registered charities and CICs only. No individuals.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Performing arts — particularly theatre and music. Youth involvement; community participation in live arts; professional development for small/medium arts orgs; freelance performing-arts workers; new writing; capital projects.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Rolling — no fixed deadlines.
funder_brief.strong_application: Demonstrate strong safeguarding, clear youth or community engagement, and the long-term resilience of the organisation.

4e036244-6f5c-4c1b-b475-129eaf4e55de.title: Social Business Trust — Strategic Growth Support
4e036244-6f5c-4c1b-b475-129eaf4e55de.description: Cash grants plus high-value pro bono business support (typically equivalent to £200k+) for scaling social enterprises and charities. Selective portfolio approach; generally requires £1m+ revenue and strong growth potential.

funder_brief.priorities: Education, employment, and health and wellbeing. They specifically seek social enterprises with the ambition to grow and scale their impact.
funder_brief.funder_tips: SBT pairs funding with seconded business expertise (e.g. from corporate partners like EY), so demonstrate openness to receiving hands-on business support alongside capital. They work closely with ambitious leaders, so a strong founding vision and track record of impact will strengthen your case.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Contact info@socialbusinesstrust.org or visit socialbusinesstrust.org for application details. Specific application process not detailed on homepage.
funder_brief.typical_award: Funding is described as 'targeted' rather than open-ended; £7m worth of expertise and funding deployed across 25 organisations in 2024/25 suggests awards are substantive but individual amounts not specified.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Social enterprises with a compelling mission, inspiring leadership, and clear growth ambition. No specific legal structure restrictions stated, but focus is on social enterprises rather than traditional charities.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Business expertise and targeted funding for social enterprises working in education, employment, and health and wellbeing. They partner with organisations to accelerate growth and amplify impact.
funder_brief.geographic_focus: UK-wide (based in London but no geographic restrictions mentioned).
funder_brief.strong_application: Organisations led by inspiring leaders with a compelling social mission and demonstrated ambition to grow. CEOs report 100% satisfaction with SBT's help in growing organisational impact, suggesting evidence of impact and willingness to engage with business support is valued.

5a368644-3211-4a40-9447-d5594938a519.title: Lambeth Community Connections Fund
5a368644-3211-4a40-9447-d5594938a519.description: £4 million Neighbourhood CIL-funded grant scheme for Lambeth-based community projects. Development Grants up to £10,000; Project Grants up to £200,000. Spent in phases over three years; projects must complete within two years of award.

funder_brief.priorities: Projects that make communities better, fairer, and safer. Funding prioritises addressing the social impact of new development and ensuring local residents benefit from sustainable growth.
funder_brief.funder_tips: This is a relatively new fund worth £4 million, raised through developer contributions. It is designed for groups with ambitious ideas, so do not be discouraged from applying if your project is bold or experimental.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Local community groups and organisations based in Lambeth. The fund is designed for grassroots groups with community ideas.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Projects led by local groups that improve communities, making them better, fairer, and safer places to live. Funding supports groups with ideas that address the impact of new development and ensure local people benefit from growth in the borough.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: The fund will be spent in phases over three years. No specific application windows or decision timelines are stated.
funder_brief.strong_application: Groups with clear, community-focused ideas that address local needs and involve residents in improving their area. Applications should demonstrate how the project responds to change or growth in Lambeth.

6c379e4b-482c-4548-9b77-bfb74dc314f8.title: Better Brighton & Hove Fund — Ward Pots 2026
6c379e4b-482c-4548-9b77-bfb74dc314f8.description: Each of the 21 Brighton & Hove wards has at least £22,000 in 2026 for community projects agreed with ward councillors. Small, local, residents-led activities welcome. Speak to your ward councillor or the council Communities team to apply.

funder_brief.funder_tips: This is a ward-based pot scheme, meaning funding is allocated by ward. Check whether your ward has available budget before applying. The council also offers support through related programmes including the Community Catalyst Fund, Fairness Fund, and Youth Led Grants Programme.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Apply through Brighton & Hove City Council's community grants portal. Visit the Community support and grants page for application details and guidance documents.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Community and voluntary organisations based in Brighton & Hove.

916f02b0-714f-4489-8528-5784c4a38cf9.title: Active Travel England — Communities and Engagement Fund
916f02b0-714f-4489-8528-5784c4a38cf9.description: Active Travel England funds projects that help more people walk, wheel and cycle. Community grants support grassroots organisations to promote active travel, remove barriers to cycling and walking, and build the local infrastructure and culture needed for more people to travel actively in England.

funder_brief.priorities: Supporting inclusive walking, wheeling and cycling schemes; behaviour change and capability building; community engagement including school programmes and training; active travel social prescribing to promote active travel for everyday journeys.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Active Travel England funds a diverse range of established organisations including Bikeability, Modeshift STARS, Big Bike Revival, and local cycle network projects. Consider whether your project fits one of their identified funding programmes or charitable partnerships.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Contact Active Travel England directly through their funding page for specific application guidance. Different funding streams (Consolidated Active Travel Fund, Active Travel Fund, Capability Fund, social prescribing pilots) have different application routes.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Local transport authorities can apply for infrastructure funding. Charities and community organisations working on active travel engagement can also receive grants. Walking, wheeling and cycling charities and organisations that work directly with local communities are eligible.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Walking, wheeling and cycling infrastructure projects, behaviour change activities, and community engagement programmes. They also fund charities and organisations working directly with communities to embed active travel in towns and cities, including school programmes, training and promotion activities.
funder_brief.strong_application: Applications should demonstrate direct community engagement and impact, alignment with local active travel plans, and evidence of how the project will embed active travel in local communities. Demonstrating behaviour change outcomes and partnership working strengthens applications.

9192771f-4c81-4761-8a59-9a39231b973c.title: Tower Hamlets — Community Grant Programme
9192771f-4c81-4761-8a59-9a39231b973c.description: £500–£10,000 for Tower Hamlets not-for-profits (income <£2M) delivering community-based projects benefitting borough residents. Three funding rounds per year; next Round 2 deadline 25 May 2026, 12:00. Applications via Blackbaud Grant Making portal.

funder_brief.priorities: Supporting and investing in a diverse voluntary and community sector. The council prioritises organisations that can demonstrate social value and contribute to the borough's economic, social and environmental wellbeing.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Apply to the programme that best matches your organisation's size and needs — the Small Grants and Emergency Fund offer faster-track options for smaller awards. Being explicit about your social value contribution strengthens your application.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Visit the Council funding for VCS page on Tower Hamlets website to access the relevant application portal for the programme you're eligible for.
funder_brief.typical_award: Three programmes operate at different levels: Mayor's Community Grants (£3.5m annually available), Mayor's Small Grants (up to unspecified individual award size from £800k annual pot, November 2023–March 2027), and Emergency Fund (up to £10,000 per application from £100k annual budget).
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Voluntary and community sector organisations registered and operating in Tower Hamlets. This includes charities, CICs, community groups and social enterprises.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Voluntary and community sector organisations across a range of causes and community needs in Tower Hamlets. The council supports diverse VCS activity through multiple grant programmes.
funder_brief.geographic_focus: Tower Hamlets only. Organisations must be working in or serving the borough.
funder_brief.strong_application: Organisations that can clearly articulate their social value impact and how they improve the borough's economic, social and environmental wellbeing will be competitive.

9ae71432-a044-4988-8eae-1f2c3223c764.title: Cambridge Social Ventures
9ae71432-a044-4988-8eae-1f2c3223c764.description: 12-month venture support programme for social entrepreneurs. Includes coaching, workshops, and access to Cambridge Judge networks.

funder_brief.exclusions: No explicit exclusions stated. However, ventures primarily focused on profit maximisation rather than social or environmental impact are unlikely to be a good fit.
funder_brief.priorities: Social and environmental impact across all sectors. They are particularly interested in ventures that address deep-rooted global social problems and those that blur boundaries between for-profit and non-profit models. The centre also focuses on peaceshaping, climate action, and inclusive, equitable solutions.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Engage with Cambridge Judge's research, faculty expertise, and existing networks early. The centre values partnerships and collaboration across sectors, so demonstrating how your venture bridges business, civil society, policy, or academia will strengthen your application. Consider attending their workshops, events, or programmes designed to support social entrepreneurs.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Visit the Cambridge Social Ventures section of the Cambridge Centre for Social Innovation website. You can explore the Social Venture Weekend, Social Venture Incubator, or sign up to the mailing list for updates on application windows and support programmes.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Entrepreneurs and venture leaders who are building social or environmental ventures. Applicants should be committed to driving their businesses forward with a focus on social or environmental impact rather than profit maximisation.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Cambridge Social Ventures supports a wide range of ventures that have positive social and environmental impacts. They fund early-stage social enterprises and ventures that aim to create real, lasting social or environmental change.
funder_brief.geographic_focus: UK-wide, with a base at Cambridge Judge Business School in Cambridge.
funder_brief.strong_application: Demonstrate a clear social or environmental mission and evidence of viable business model development. Applicants with experience in the Cambridge Social Ventures programmes (such as the Social Venture Weekend or Incubator) or those who have engaged with Cambridge Judge's research and networks will be well-positioned.

eligibility_criteria: Access to coaching, workshops, and Cambridge Judge networks

9e63bf54-8956-4816-b32d-d164f99ab0ea.title: Chichester City Council — Community Grants
9e63bf54-8956-4816-b32d-d164f99ab0ea.description: Parish-level community grants for voluntary, community and not-for-profit organisations delivering activities benefitting Chichester city residents. Separate from (and smaller scale than) Chichester District Council's grants programme.

funder_brief.exclusions: For-profit organisations. Organisations whose work is not substantially focused on or based in Chichester. Large/core funding grants are currently closed (as of the latest update).
funder_brief.priorities: Supporting community-based activity and organisations that serve the local Chichester population.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Large/core funding grants are currently fully allocated — focus on Community Grants for one-off projects. For larger projects beyond the scope of grants, contact the council to ask about alternative funding sources. Read the Grants and Free Use policy before applying.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Download the application form and guidance notes (2026-2027). Complete the form with supporting paperwork and submit by email to administration@chichestercity.gov.uk or by post to Chichester City Council, The Council House, North Street, Chichester, PO19 1LQ.
funder_brief.typical_award: Community Grants: up to £3,000 for one-off projects, events or activities. Large Grants: up to £5,000 per year for core running costs (currently closed to new applications). Free Use: provision of council facilities at no cost.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Non-profit making organisations based in Chichester or whose work is mainly focused within the Parish of Chichester. This includes registered charities, community groups, and CICs.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: One-off projects, events, activities, and core running costs for community organisations. Also offers free use of council facilities to eligible groups.
funder_brief.geographic_focus: Chichester city and the Parish of Chichester only.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Applications are considered on a rolling basis at quarterly Community Affairs Committee meetings. Check the City Council website for the meeting calendar for specific decision dates.
funder_brief.strong_application: Applications should clearly demonstrate how the project or organisation benefits the Chichester community. Follow the published guidelines carefully and provide supporting documentation.

a9364402-f2a3-45b0-bf80-d33d9e5efdf5.title: Brighton & Hove — Community Catalyst Fund (2027–2029)
a9364402-f2a3-45b0-bf80-d33d9e5efdf5.description: Two-year core funding programme for Brighton & Hove not-for-profit organisations, reflecting Council Plan priorities and supporting resilience through the provision of 2-year grants. The 2027–2029 round is expected to open for applications in autumn 2026.

funder_brief.exclusions: Organisations that can redistribute profits to shareholders or members. Organisations with annual income over £500,000.
funder_brief.priorities: A City To Be Proud Of (sustainable environment, safer place, prospering economy); A Fair and Inclusive City (fairness, accessibility, inclusion, safety); A Healthy City Where People Thrive (residents living and ageing well, children and young people's futures).
funder_brief.funder_tips: This fund explicitly supports 2-year funding to build organisational resilience. Core costs are funded alongside project costs, so don't hesitate to include staffing and running expenses. Review the funded projects list to see the kinds of organisations and activities that succeed.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Apply through the council's grants portal. Applications should address at least one outcome, demonstrate local delivery experience, show evidence of need, and explain equal opportunities safeguards.
funder_brief.typical_award: Up to £10,000 per year for organisations meeting the income threshold. Actual awards in the 2025–2027 round ranged from £1,000 to £20,000.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Local community groups, voluntary organisations, and not-for-profit social enterprises with an annual income up to £500,000. Organisations with capacity to redistribute profits to shareholders or members are ineligible. You can apply individually or in partnership.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Core running costs and project costs for community groups, voluntary organisations, and not-for-profit social enterprises delivering activities that align with the council's priorities around sustainability, fairness, inclusion, and health.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: The 2027–2029 round is expected to open in autumn 2026. The 2025–2027 round received 108 applications and funded 45 projects.
funder_brief.strong_application: Clearly demonstrate experience delivering in Brighton & Hove, show evidence of community need, and explain how your activity ensures equal opportunities. Address at least one of the three council outcomes explicitly.

eligibility_criteria: Local community groups, voluntary organisations, and not-for-profit social enterprises with an annual income up to £500,000
Organisations with capacity to redistribute profits to shareholders or members are ineligible
You can apply individually or in partnership

b3086bff-58af-4ffa-836c-855cf136a499.title: Vicar's Relief Fund — St Martin-in-the-Fields Charity
b3086bff-58af-4ffa-836c-855cf136a499.description: Emergency crisis grants up to £350 for people at risk of or experiencing homelessness. Frontline agencies apply on behalf of beneficiaries for rent arrears, deposits, essential goods; fast turnaround, rolling.

funder_brief.exclusions: Individuals cannot apply directly — only support workers and frontline staff can make applications on behalf of service users.
funder_brief.priorities: Urgent housing access for people facing homelessness. The fund prioritises individuals who need to secure a place to live quickly and lack funds for essential upfront costs like deposits.
funder_brief.funder_tips: This fund is designed for speed — grants can transform someone's circumstances within days. Work directly with your service users to understand their specific barriers to housing, and be clear about the exact upfront costs needed (deposit, emergency accommodation, ID, moving costs).
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Support workers apply through the grant portal. Help information and guidance on the application process is available on their website.
funder_brief.typical_award: Up to £500 per grant
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Support workers and frontline staff can apply on behalf of individuals they support who are facing homelessness. Applications are made through a grant portal by experienced frontline workers.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Emergency grants to help individuals experiencing homelessness secure urgent accommodation. Grants cover essential upfront costs including rental deposits, emergency accommodation, ID documents, and moving costs.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Grants are issued quickly via experienced frontline staff; no specific decision timeline provided
funder_brief.strong_application: Applications from experienced frontline workers who understand the urgent needs of their service users and can demonstrate how the grant will directly help someone access safe accommodation.

eligibility_criteria: Frontline homelessness agency applies on behalf of client

b7656b4f-58dd-427d-81d5-c1961b0a0f77.title: Foundation Scotland — Social Investment Fund
b7656b4f-58dd-427d-81d5-c1961b0a0f77.description: Social investment for community organisations in Scotland. Provides patient capital and blended finance for community enterprises.

funder_brief.priorities: Community wellbeing, fairness, and sustainability. They emphasise supporting the building blocks of communities and enabling social enterprises to grow and deliver positive social impact.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Foundation Scotland emphasises partnership and understanding your community's needs. They offer tailored support to help organisations maximise funding opportunities. Consider approaching them early for application advice.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Visit their 'Apply for funding' section to view available grants. They provide support with applications and recommend contacting them directly for guidance on which fund suits your project.
funder_brief.typical_award: Grants range from under £1,000 (some community funds offer up to £1,000) to larger awards. Recent grants distributed averaged across 3,195 awards from £20.9m annually, suggesting a mix of small to mid-sized grants.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Registered charities, community groups, social enterprises, and CICs across Scotland. No minimum income requirement stated.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Projects and initiatives that make communities happier, fairer, and more sustainable. They support charities, community groups, and social enterprises across a range of causes through both grants and social investment.
funder_brief.geographic_focus: Scotland-wide. They work with all Scottish communities and also manage place-based community benefit funds from the renewables sector.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Not specified. They distribute funding through 285 different funds, each likely with its own timeline.
funder_brief.strong_application: Applications that clearly show how the project benefits the local community and demonstrates genuine community need. Organisations that can articulate their social impact are more competitive.

eligibility_criteria: Social enterprise or community enterprise focus
Patient capital or blended finance eligible

c1a86516-b4be-4535-90cc-4a672750d652.title: Pilotlight — Pro Bono Support Matching
c1a86516-b4be-4535-90cc-4a672750d652.description: Matches charities, CICs and social enterprises with pro bono strategic expertise from skilled business volunteers. Non-cash support across strategy, marketing, HR, operations, finance; typically 6-month engagements for Pilotlighters + pro bono programmes.

funder_brief.priorities: Building resilience and strategic vision in charities; developing leadership skills; creating sustainable partnerships between business and the charity sector; addressing real-world challenges in communities; supporting climate action and social impact.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Charities working with Pilotlight 360 increase income by an average of 48% within two years. Programmes have a 98% satisfaction rating from charity participants. They value organisations ready to engage seriously with strategic development and able to work collaboratively with business volunteers.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Visit the 'For Charities' section and 'Apply for support' on their website. Specific application process details should be available there or by contacting Pilotlight directly.
funder_brief.typical_award: Not a traditional grant programme — Pilotlight matches charities with pro bono business expertise and support rather than awarding cash grants. The Pilotlight 360 programme appears to be their flagship offering for strategic development.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Registered charities and social organisations. No explicit income caps or stage restrictions mentioned, but their focus is on charity leaders and organisations seeking strategic development support.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Pilotlight provides pro bono business expertise and strategic support to charities and social organisations. They match charities with volunteer business professionals to help develop leadership, sharpen strategy, build partnerships, and increase organisational impact and income.
funder_brief.geographic_focus: UK-wide, with particular presence in London and Glasgow.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Not explicitly stated. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis; contact Pilotlight directly for current timescales.
funder_brief.strong_application: Charities with clear strategic challenges or leadership development needs, openness to working with business volunteers, and ambition to grow impact and income. Organisations that can engage leadership teams in the process tend to see strongest results.

d881ca00-a65b-4326-a918-34e75ea648a0.title: Social Firms Wales
d881ca00-a65b-4326-a918-34e75ea648a0.description: Support for social firms and social enterprises in Wales. Provides training, networking, and business development resources.

funder_brief.priorities: Creating thriving employment opportunities where people feel valued, included and useful. Supporting enterprise development that combines business viability with social impact and fair employment practices.
funder_brief.funder_tips: Social Firms Wales positions itself as a 'critical friend' — they value honest dialogue. Make use of their free weekly newsletter for grant updates and learning from other members. Consider joining their membership to access their network and buy-from-members opportunities, which can support your business sustainability alongside grant funding.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Contact Social Firms Wales directly to discuss your idea or business need. They offer support through consultancy, funding advice, and grants. Use their 'Getting ready to apply for funding' resources and 'Grants for social enterprises' or 'Grants for self-employed entrepreneurs' guides. They provide one-to-one support to help you prepare applications.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Individuals and organisations wanting to adopt social firms principles. This includes self-employed entrepreneurs, social enterprises, and community-based businesses. Legal structure not explicitly restricted.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Social enterprises and businesses that prioritise fair employment and equity. They support organisations adopting social firms principles — placing equity at the centre of their employment practice.
funder_brief.strong_application: Organisations with genuine commitment to social firms principles and equitable employment. Demonstrating a clear business idea or existing operation seeking growth. Being open to honest, critical feedback on your approach.

eligibility_criteria: Social firm or social enterprise in Wales

e0ed3c06-8488-45bf-8514-b06b16019161.title: Cripplegate Foundation — Islington Community Chest
e0ed3c06-8488-45bf-8514-b06b16019161.description: Up to £5,000 a year for Islington voluntary organisations working with residents experiencing poverty or isolation. Priority given to organisations with turnover under £50,000; maximum applicant turnover £100,000. Runs in twice-yearly rounds.

funder_brief.exclusions: Organisations with annual turnover of £100,000 or more cannot apply. You cannot apply more than once per year.
funder_brief.priorities: Empowering Lives (inclusive, affordable support and enriching activities); Greener, Healthier Islington (mental and physical wellbeing, outdoor spaces); Community Wealth Building (financial resilience, jobs access); Child-Friendly Islington (equal opportunities for all children); A Safe Place to Call Home (safety, homelessness support, violence against women and girls support).
funder_brief.funder_tips: This is a relational funding programme — the panel values genuine connection to Islington's communities. A 59% success rate in 2024/25 suggests strong chances if you meet the criteria. Plan your project timeline carefully as there's an eight-week gap between application deadline and decision. After funding, actively tell your local councillors and supporters about the grant and add the ICCC logo to your materials.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Download the guidance document and budget form (available as PDF or Word). Complete and submit via the online portal by noon on the deadline date. You can save incomplete applications and return to them. Contact the Programme Manager or Voluntary Action Islington for support.
funder_brief.typical_award: Up to £5,000 per year.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Islington-based voluntary organisations and community groups with annual turnover under £100,000 (priority given to those under £50,000). Community Interest Companies (CICs) can apply but should consult separate guidance. You can only apply once per year regardless of previous success.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Small grants for voluntary and community organisations working with Islington residents experiencing poverty and/or isolation. Projects should align with Council priorities: inclusive support and activities, mental and physical wellbeing, financial resilience and employment, child opportunities, or support for homelessness and violence against women and girls.
funder_brief.geographic_focus: Islington only. Your organisation must work with Islington residents.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Two application rounds per year. Next deadline: 16 February 2026 (decisions by 14 April 2026); following deadline: 21 September 2026 (decisions by 10 November 2026). Panel meets at least eight weeks after each deadline. Funding is released within one month of Terms and Conditions being signed.
funder_brief.strong_application: The application panel includes local councillors, foundation governors, voluntary sector members and residents — they value organisations rooted in community needs and understanding of local isolation or poverty. Clear alignment with one or more Council priorities and realistic budgets strengthen applications.

eligibility_criteria: Islington-based voluntary organisations and community groups with annual turnover under £100,000 (priority given to those under £50,000)
Community Interest Companies (CICs) can apply but should consult separate guidance
You can only apply once per year regardless of previous success

e72200b0-f3df-44d2-85bc-a55b5d2aa0a4.title: Harold Hyam Wingate Foundation — Music & Performing Arts
e72200b0-f3df-44d2-85bc-a55b5d2aa0a4.description: Grants for small UK-registered charities working in music, performing arts, and Jewish/interfaith relations. Aims to support activity that creates significant impact on individuals and/or communities and leaves a lasting legacy.

funder_brief.priorities: Music; performing arts; Jewish/interfaith relations.
funder_brief.funder_tips: A funding-criteria update was implemented in July 2025 — re-read the criteria before applying.
funder_brief.how_to_apply: Email completed application form to admin@wingate.org.uk. Instructions and forms at wingate.org.uk/apply/. Next deadline: Friday 21 August 2026 at 5pm.
funder_brief.typical_award: Not published; check directly.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: UK-registered charities — smaller organisations preferred.
funder_brief.what_they_fund: Music, performing arts, and Jewish/interfaith activity that creates significant impact and lasting legacy.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: Decisions follow each deadline; one main annual round.

eligibility_criteria: Working in music, performing arts, or Jewish/interfaith relations

f1c42af9-3659-4b39-8fb5-4c00a8f5ce7e.title: Southwark Council — Neighbourhood Grants
f1c42af9-3659-4b39-8fb5-4c00a8f5ce7e.description: Neighbourhood Grants from £500 (small events and projects) to £50,000 (contributions to larger construction works). Funded through developer contributions for local improvements.

funder_brief.exclusions: No explicit exclusions stated, but Pride Fund events must take place between June and end of August; Black History Month grants are for October events; and some funds (like Getting Involved Grants) are restricted to specific organisation types.
funder_brief.priorities: Projects that create cleaner, greener, safer neighbourhoods; support LGBTQI+ communities and cultural celebrations; promote inclusive and equitable arts and culture; support regular sport and physical activity for less active people; and improve wellbeing in council housing communities.

brief.what_they_fund: Community projects that improve residents' lives and neighbourhoods in Southwark. Funding streams include: Cleaner Greener Safer projects, Devolved Highways improvements, Neighbourhoods Fund projects, public art, LGBTQI+ Pride events, Black History Month celebrations, arts and culture projects, community celebrations, sport and physical activity programmes, and local activities for council housing residents.
brief.who_can_apply: Open to constituted organisations, tenant and resident associations (TRAs), charities, clubs, residents, and individuals who live or work in Southwark. Some streams have specific eligibility: Southwark Pride Fund and Black History Month open to event organisers; Culture Together Fund open to arts and culture organisations; Active Southwark Olympic Legacy Fund open to local organisations; Getting Involved Grants open to TRAs, Tenant Management Organisations (TMOs), or local groups for council housing tenants and homeowners.
brief.geographic_focus: Southwark only. All projects and events must take place in Southwark.
brief.priorities: Community cohesion and thriving neighbourhoods; inclusive and equitable cultural sector; sustainability of arts and culture organisations; recovery from COVID-19 impact; regular participation in sport and physical activity, especially for people unable to be active regularly; wellbeing of council housing residents.
brief.strong_application: Applications should demonstrate clear community benefit and resident impact. Public art projects should follow the council's public art guidance. Events should be deliverable within funding stream timescales (e.g. Pride events June–August, Black History Month in October). Applications should show how they address council priorities such as community cohesion, environmental improvement, or accessibility to activity.
brief.exclusions: Source does not explicitly state exclusions beyond the requirement that projects must take place in Southwark and meet the specific criteria of each funding stream.
brief.typical_award: Range varies by funding stream: £500–£50,000 for Neighbourhood Grants (small events/projects at £500, larger construction contributions at £50,000); up to £2,499 for Southwark Pride Fund; up to £2,499 for Black History Month; up to £4,000 (small grants) or £4,001–£10,000 (large grants) for Cultural Celebrations Fund. Exact awards for Culture Together Fund and Active Southwark Olympic Legacy Fund not specified.
brief.decision_timeline: Source does not specify decision timescales or trustee meeting dates. For opening and closing dates, applicants are directed to a separate information page.
brief.how_to_apply: Application is made through a single combined online process for Cleaner Greener Safer, Devolved Highways, and Neighbourhoods Fund streams. Public art projects should follow separate public art guidance. Applicants should refer to the council's grants information page for specific programme guidance and application details.
brief.funder_tips: Read the specific guidance for your funding stream, particularly if applying for public art. Multiple funding streams are now combined into one application process, simplifying the process for those applying across themes.

brief.what_they_fund: Fast emergency grants to help people experiencing or at risk of homelessness access safe accommodation. Grants cover specific costs including rent deposits, rent in advance, ID fees, moving costs, and temporary accommodation costs.

brief.priorities: Preventing homelessness and helping people secure safe homes. Supporting individuals experiencing mental health challenges, domestic abuse survivors, and people rebuilding lives after housing loss.
brief.strong_application: Applications are strongest when submitted by experienced frontline support workers with existing relationships and credibility with clients. brief.exclusions: Applications from members of the public, volunteers, or individuals applying on their own behalf are not accepted. Only paid frontline workers can submit grant requests.
brief.typical_award: Up to £650 per grant to help people access accommodation.
brief.decision_timeline: Grants are issued quickly and efficiently via experienced support workers, though specific decision timescales are not detailed.
brief.how_to_apply: Support workers seeking to apply should click the application link on the Vicar's Relief Fund page to make an application on behalf of an individual they are supporting.
brief.funder_tips: This fund prioritises speed and efficiency—grants are processed rapidly through frontline workers who know their clients well. Strong applications include clear evidence of the specific costs being claimed. The funder values established partnerships with frontline organisations and works with workers who have credibility and experience supporting people into housing.
